hook_text: Every rand a business earns or spends starts its life as a scrap of paper. Here is the shoebox that proves it.
clip_script: A plumber's bakkie, a shoebox on the passenger seat. Inside: the carbon copy of a cash invoice for a geyser repair, money in. A receipt book with copies, money in. The till roll from the workshop counter with the day's total, money in. A deposit slip proving the notes reached the bank. A proof of payment for pipes paid by EFT, money out. A hardware shop cash slip, money out. And at month-end, the bank statement, listing everything, even bank charges nobody handed him on paper. Receipts, till slips, deposit slips, EFTs, bank statements, cash invoices: the six source documents. The rule? Give a document away, keep the bottom copy. Get one, keep the top copy. And keep them five years, because SARS can ask.
visual_style: A whiteboard bakkie with a shoebox, each document pulled out, labelled and dropped onto a money-in or money-out pile, ending with a calendar marked five years.
mood: Practical and slightly detective-like, paper becoming proof.
pacing: Quick document-by-document pull from the box, a pause on the copy rule, a firm last line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort every document into the right journal.
